response:
Evidence-based redirection: the archive now separates cleanly into two families. Additive/monotone composites (gen-0 rank sums, industry z-score differences, the cheapness-weighted inventory signal) generate strong FMB slopes and even a good raw Sharpe (0.37) but zero-or-negative FF5 alpha — their spread is HML+CMA. The *leg-matched conditional* family is the only one producing positive FF5 alpha, and within it the discriminating variable matters enormously: capex-to-installed-plant intensity gave +4.2% alpha (t=2.2, FMB 2.35), cumulative acquisition spending gave +1.6% (t=1.4, FMB 2.36), while vintage, payout split, instability, and internal-cash-claim variants all failed on the FMB sign or produced negligible alpha. Two diagnosed weaknesses remain in the winner: its raw Sharpe is ~0, so the alpha comes from factor-loading offset rather than a paying spread, and its 70% zero mass makes the tails thin. This batch attacks exactly those two problems (breadth via two-tail gating and continuous weighting, paying spread via combining the alpha-producing and Sharpe-producing interactions) and adds channels — physical replacement-cost cheapness, capacity sweating, and headcount discipline — that extend the interaction to asset-light firms the capx/ppent leg cannot describe.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Reinvestment Discipline In Both Valuation Tails
EXPRESSION: MUL(ADD(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), INDICATOR(NEG(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), -0.3)), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(capx, ppent)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Reinvestment intensity is informative about returns only where price expectations are extreme — among deep-value firms it separates harvesters from value traps, and among glamour firms it separates asset-light compounders from empire builders — while for middling valuations capital spending carries no mispricing content.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This doubles the informative mass of the archive's best design from 30% to 60% of the universe, directly fixing the thin-tail and degenerate-breakpoint problem the critic identified, and it does so by adding an economically motivated second gate rather than by nudging a percentile. It is also a diagnostic: if alpha survives or strengthens, the interaction lives in both valuation tails; if it collapses, the mispricing is specific to the value side and future work should stay there.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Dual Channel Discipline Fixed Plus Working Capital
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(capx, ppent)), 1))), MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(GROWTH(RATIO(invt, sale), 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital discipline in cheap firms shows up in two economically independent places — the fixed-asset program and the working-capital cycle — and a firm restrained on both dimensions is a far more credible disciplined allocator than one restrained on either alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two components are the archive's two best but complementary results: the gated capx signal supplies FF5 alpha with no raw spread, while the cheapness-weighted inventory signal supplies the best raw Sharpe (0.37) with no alpha, so aggregating their ranks tests whether the paying spread and the abnormal return can be obtained simultaneously rather than one at a time. Note that both inputs are already interactions, so this is not a value-plus-investment rank sum of the kind that repeatedly failed; it is a diversification across two interaction channels.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Replacement Cost Cheapness With Reinvestment Restraint
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ppegt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(capx, ppent)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness anchored on physical capacity — market value per dollar of gross installed plant, a crude replacement-cost multiple — identifies firms trading below the cost of rebuilding their asset base, and among these the ones not adding further capacity are the genuinely underappreciated disciplined operators.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This changes the valuation anchor from accounting book equity, which is distorted by write-downs, buybacks, and leverage, to gross physical capital at historical cost, so the gate now identifies low Tobin-q-on-capacity firms rather than low-book-to-price firms and the resulting long leg is not a repackaged HML portfolio. Because both the gate and the discriminator are built from investment-account variables while price supplies the valuation side, the signal is a genuine q-theory statement: cheap relative to installed capacity and refusing to add more.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Capacity Sweating Within Cheap Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), WINSOR(ZSCORE(GROWTH(RATIO(sale, ppegt), 1)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Disciplined allocation means getting more revenue out of the capacity you already own; among cheap firms, rising sales per dollar of gross plant signals management sweating existing assets instead of building new ones, and the market underestimates how much free cash that generates.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the utilization dimension rather than the spending dimension: the same low-capex firm can be starving a shrinking business or squeezing more output from installed capacity, and only the second is a disciplined allocator, so the signal targets a distinction the archive's level and change-in-level signals cannot make. It uses gross rather than net plant so the ratio is not mechanically inflated by depreciation, which is what corrupted the asset-vintage test that produced a wrong-signed slope.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Headcount Restraint Within Cheap Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(GROWTH(emp, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: For the large share of cheap firms whose real capacity is people rather than plant, discipline is visible in hiring: value firms expanding headcount are committing to growth the market is not paying for, while those holding headcount flat are converting existing operations into cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The capx-to-plant discriminator that produced the archive's alpha is nearly meaningless for asset-light firms, so this extends the same leg-matched structure to the labor input and tests whether investment discipline is an input-general phenomenon or specific to physical capital. Unlike the earlier labor proposal, which was an additive productivity composite contaminated by layoff-driven margin gains, this uses the hiring decision itself as the discipline variable inside a value-matched gate.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Continuous Cheapness Weighted Reinvestment Penalty
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(capx, ppent)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The penalty for heavy reinvestment should scale smoothly with how little the market is paying for the firm's book value, so cheapness acts as a continuous amplifier of investment discipline rather than an on-off eligibility condition.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates one design choice against the archive's best signal — hard percentile gate versus continuous bounded weight — while keeping the economic content identical, which matters because the gated version had essentially zero raw Sharpe and derived its alpha from factor-loading offset on thin tails. Full-universe coverage with no zero mass should stabilize decile composition and, if the mechanism is real rather than an artifact of a 15% tail, improve the FMB slope and the alpha t-stat together.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Reinvestment Discipline In Both Valuation Tails---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The two-sided gate is internally consistent (both indicators evaluate correctly, and the asset-growth anomaly predicts the same sign in the glamour tail), and it is a genuine diagnostic rather than a percentile nudge, though it risks diluting the archive's alpha by pooling cheap and expensive low-capex firms into the same extreme deciles with a large zero mass in the middle.

---CRITIQUE Dual Channel Discipline Fixed Plus Working Capital---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical rank-blend of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content, and it is technically fragile because the gated capx component is exactly zero for 70% of firms, so its rank contribution is a giant tie block that will dominate the sum and mostly reproduce the inventory signal.

---CRITIQUE Replacement Cost Cheapness With Reinvestment Restraint---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Swapping the valuation anchor from book equity to gross installed plant is a substantive change that produces a low-q-on-capacity gate rather than a repackaged HML long leg, though the gate will load heavily on capital-intensive industries and is partly mechanically related to the capx/ppent discriminator, so industry neutralization would be the natural next refinement.

---CRITIQUE Capacity Sweating Within Cheap Firms---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The utilization-versus-spending distinction is economically real and not covered by the archive's level and change-in-level capex signals, but the discriminator is essentially the change in asset turnover (Soliman's DuPont decomposition, a published predictor) and can rise mechanically from divestitures rather than sweating assets, so the result will need a disposal control to be interpretable.

---CRITIQUE Headcount Restraint Within Cheap Firms---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The discriminator is the well-documented hiring-rate/employment-growth anomaly (Bazdresch-Belo-Lin, Belo-Lin-Bazdresch), so the proposal is that known factor conditioned on value rather than a new mechanism, and the emp field is annual, frequently stale and rounded, which will inject noise into precisely the asset-light firms the design is meant to reach.

---CRITIQUE Continuous Cheapness Weighted Reinvestment Penalty---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The proposal itself concedes the economic content is identical to the archive's best signal and only the gate-versus-weight encoding changes, which is the definition of a cosmetic variant; worse, multiplying a signed z-score by a strictly positive rank makes the composite a capex-discipline signal with an amplitude tilt rather than a value-investment interaction, so it cannot cleanly test the stated mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Total Operating Capital Absorption Within Cheap Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), ADD(ppent, invt))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: What drains a cheap firm's distributable cash is the total capital it absorbs, fixed plus working, so the right discipline measure is combined capital absorption per dollar of operating capital already employed; firms with low total absorption are harvesters and those with high absorption are consuming the very cash flow the low multiple is supposed to represent.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Instead of blending the ranks of two evaluated signals, this builds a single new accounting quantity — capex plus the change in inventory over plant plus inventory — which is the firm's total incremental claim on operating capital and is not the sum of two previously tested sorts. Because the denominator includes inventory, the measure is meaningful for distribution- and retail-type value firms whose capital is in stock rather than plant, extending the winning mechanism to firms where capx/ppent is uninformative, and no giant tie block enters the construction beyond the intended valuation gate.
REASONING_NOTE: Positive denominator by construction, so no explosive scaling.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Capital Deepening Against Labor Within Cheap Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(GROWTH(RATIO(ppent, emp), 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Irreversibility is the cost of aggressive investment: a cheaply valued firm that raises capital per worker is substituting sunk, non-recoverable plant for flexible labor precisely when the market says its growth options are worth little, and it loses the ability to shrink cheaply if demand disappoints.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The discriminator is the capital-labor mix, not the hiring rate — headcount growth enters the ratio with the opposite sign to plant growth, so a firm that hires while holding plant flat scores as disciplined here and as undisciplined under the employment-growth anomaly, which makes this a distinct and partly opposing prediction rather than a known factor conditioned on value. Framing discipline as commitment irreversibility also explains why the level of spending matters more for value firms, whose depressed multiples imply little option value in new capacity, and ratio-of-levels construction is less sensitive to stale or rounded employment counts than a headcount growth rate alone.
REASONING_NOTE: Uses plant per employee, so both the investment and the labor input enter as a single economic quantity.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Expansion Overhang Within Cheap Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), NEG(WINSOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(LAG(capx, 2), ppent)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The damage from aggressive investment is felt with a lag: a cheap firm whose heavy spending occurred two years ago is now carrying capacity built for demand that did not arrive, and that overhang depresses future margins and returns, whereas a cheap firm that was already restrained two years ago has no such legacy to absorb.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This introduces a timing dimension the archive has never tested — every prior investment leg used contemporaneous levels or one-year changes — so the comparison with the archive's best signal directly identifies whether the mispricing is about current capital discipline or about the unrecognized legacy of past expansion, which is the economically more plausible story since capacity built earlier only shows up in realized profitability later. It is not a reweighting of the winner: past and current reinvestment rates are far from collinear, and the design deliberately allows a firm currently spending heavily to be classified as clean if its prior expansion was modest.
REASONING_NOTE: Only a two-year lag is required, so coverage should stay near the archive's 0.12-0.13 range.
